# tellus

> tellus is an actor framework for Rust, built on Tokio: typed actors as state machines, supervision trees, a death watch with an ordering guarantee, event sourcing and clustering. The crate is `tellus` on crates.io; PostgreSQL stores for event sourcing are in the separate crate `tellus-persistence-postgres`, DNS and Kubernetes seed discovery in `tellus-bootstrap-dns` and `tellus-bootstrap-k8s`, and an HTTP view of a node's cluster state in `tellus-cluster-inspect`.

Key facts for writing tellus code:

- Message handlers are synchronous. `Actor::receive(&self, context: &ActorContext<M>, incoming: Incoming<M>, state: State) -> Result<Control<State>, Error>` is a plain function, not an `async fn`. It takes the state by value and returns `Control::Continue(next_state)` or `Control::Stop`. Never await or block inside `receive`.
- Async work runs outside the handler: `context.pipe_to_self(future, into_message)` runs a future on a new Tokio task and delivers its output as a message. Blocking work goes into `tokio::task::spawn_blocking` the same way.
- `ActorRef::tell(message)` never blocks and never fails visibly; undeliverable messages are logged at warn level as dead letters. `ActorRef::ask(within, |reply_to| Message::Get(reply_to))` is async and meant for code outside actors. Between actors, `context.reply_to(into_message)` creates a `ReplyTo` whose reply arrives as an ordinary message.
- Child actors are created with `context.spawn(actor)` or `context.spawn_with_config(actor, config)`. `context.watch(&actor_ref)` delivers `Incoming::Terminated(actor_id)` after every message that actor delivered to the watcher. Across nodes that holds for a real termination; a signal synthesized when a node is downed only guarantees that nothing more from that actor arrives, and a few other synthesized signals guarantee not even that.
- `ActorConfig` holds the mailbox capacity and the supervision strategy. Mailboxes are unbounded by default, but a bounded mailbox (`MailboxCapacity::Bounded`) is recommended; a full mailbox drops the newest message, except terminated signals, `reply_to` replies and the outputs of piped futures, which pass the capacity. `SupervisionStrategy::Stop` is the default; `Restart(RestartPolicy::new(max_restarts))` re-runs `init` with exponential backoff.
- Event sourcing (feature `persistence`): implement `EventSourced`, where `handle` returns an `Effect` naming the events to persist and `apply` folds an event into the state. Spawn the root with `ActorSystem::event_sourced(actor, persistence)`. Feature `persistence-in-memory` adds `InMemoryStore`.
- Clustering (feature `cluster`; `cluster-dev` adds `QuicTransport::dev`, which checks no certificates, for local use): one endpoint per process with `cluster::start_endpoint(EndpointConfig::new(advertised_addr), transport)`, then `cluster::bootstrap(seeds, BootstrapConfig::new())`, or `cluster::form()` and `cluster::join(&seeds)`. `ActorRef` and `ReplyTo` are serializable, and `tell`, `ask` and `watch` work across nodes through the same API. Messages that cross the wire derive serde `Serialize` and `Deserialize`; a message type looked up by key also implements `Manifest`. `cluster::register(&Key::new(name), &actor_ref)` registers an actor, `receptionist::lookup`, `lookup_at` and `subscribe` find it. Production uses mutual TLS, `QuicTransport::mutual_tls` or `QuicTransport::from_config`. A node leaves with `cluster::leave_on_terminated(system)` and exits when it is downed.
- Feature `test-util` adds `testing::TestContext` to unit test `receive`, `handle` and `apply` without an actor system. Feature `serde` makes `ActorConfig` deserializable from configuration files.

## Tutorials

- [Getting started](https://tellus.rs/docs/tutorials/getting-started/): Your first actors: messages, a tree of actors, watch, supervision and timers.
- [Hello, tellus](https://tellus.rs/docs/tutorials/getting-started/hello/): Create an actor system with a single actor that handles one message and stops.
- [A device actor](https://tellus.rs/docs/tutorials/getting-started/device/): Keep state in an actor, tell it readings and ask it for the last one.
- [A group of devices](https://tellus.rs/docs/tutorials/getting-started/group/): Spawn child actors on demand and route messages to them.
- [Watching devices](https://tellus.rs/docs/tutorials/getting-started/watch/): Learn when an actor has terminated, and rely on having seen all of its messages.
- [Asking all devices](https://tellus.rs/docs/tutorials/getting-started/query/): Collect answers from many actors with a short-lived query actor, without timeouts.
- [When devices fail](https://tellus.rs/docs/tutorials/getting-started/supervision/): Let failing actors restart with backoff, and stop them when they keep failing.
- [A device manager](https://tellus.rs/docs/tutorials/getting-started/device-manager/): Put a manager on top of the groups and route commands through the actor tree.
- [Stale readings](https://tellus.rs/docs/tutorials/getting-started/stale-readings/): Let devices forget old readings with a timer, which an actor opts into by its type.
- [Event-sourced actors](https://tellus.rs/docs/tutorials/event-sourced-actors/): Make the devices survive restarts with event sourcing, in memory first, then in PostgreSQL.
- [An event-sourced device](https://tellus.rs/docs/tutorials/event-sourced-actors/device/): Persist readings as events and recover the last one in a new actor system.
- [When devices fail, again](https://tellus.rs/docs/tutorials/event-sourced-actors/supervision/): Let a failing event-sourced device restart and recover its state by replay.
- [Snapshots](https://tellus.rs/docs/tutorials/event-sourced-actors/snapshots/): Shorten recovery with snapshots, so a device does not replay its whole history.
- [PostgreSQL](https://tellus.rs/docs/tutorials/event-sourced-actors/postgres/): Store the device's events and snapshots in PostgreSQL and recover them across processes.
- [Clustered actors](https://tellus.rs/docs/tutorials/clustered-actors/): Run the device manager on several nodes: bootstrap, the receptionist, remote ask and remote watch.
- [Two nodes](https://tellus.rs/docs/tutorials/clustered-actors/two-nodes/): Start two nodes that find each other through a list of seeds and form a cluster.
- [Messages that travel](https://tellus.rs/docs/tutorials/clustered-actors/remotable-messages/): Move the device manager to a node of its own and send it readings and questions across the wire.
- [Finding the device manager](https://tellus.rs/docs/tutorials/clustered-actors/receptionist/): Find the device manager by its key alone, wherever it runs, through the receptionist.
- [When a node dies](https://tellus.rs/docs/tutorials/clustered-actors/remote-watch/): Watch a device manager on another node, kill its node and turn to a second device manager.
- [Leaving gracefully](https://tellus.rs/docs/tutorials/clustered-actors/leave/): Stop a device manager on request and let its node leave the cluster instead of being killed.

## How-to guides

- [Call async code from an actor](https://tellus.rs/docs/how-to/call-async-code/): Run a database query or an HTTP request for an actor and get the result back as a message.
- [Unit test an actor](https://tellus.rs/docs/how-to/unit-test/): Test receive, handle and apply as plain functions with TestContext, without an actor system.
- [Configure an actor from a file](https://tellus.rs/docs/how-to/configure-supervision/): Load mailbox capacity and supervision from a config file instead of hard-coding them.
- [Apply backpressure](https://tellus.rs/docs/how-to/apply-backpressure/): Keep a fast producer from overwhelming slow actors with work pulling, and bound mailboxes safely.
- [Batch writes](https://tellus.rs/docs/how-to/batch-writes/): Write buffered entries in batches, without blocking, starting a write once the mailbox has run empty.
- [Run on Kubernetes](https://tellus.rs/docs/how-to/run-on-kubernetes/): Run cluster nodes as pods: advertise the pod's address, find the peers by label, report readiness and leave on termination.
- [Shut down gracefully](https://tellus.rs/docs/how-to/shut-down-gracefully/): Take a node out of the load balancer's rotation, drain its requests, leave the cluster and exit.
- [Observe a cluster](https://tellus.rs/docs/how-to/observe-a-cluster/): Follow the membership as it changes, and serve a node's view of its cluster over HTTP.
- [Secure with mutual TLS](https://tellus.rs/docs/how-to/secure-with-mutual-tls/): Authenticate every node with a certificate from the cluster's own certificate authority, bound to its address.

## Explanation

- [The actor model in Rust](https://tellus.rs/docs/explanation/actor-model/): What actors are, why they suit Rust's ownership rules, and when tasks, channels or locks are the better choice.
- [Actors as state machines](https://tellus.rs/docs/explanation/state-machines/): Why the state is passed into receive and returned from it, and how that models a state machine.
- [Synchronous message handlers](https://tellus.rs/docs/explanation/synchronous-handlers/): Why receive is a plain function, and what that means for your code.
- [Message delivery](https://tellus.rs/docs/explanation/message-delivery/): What tellus guarantees about delivering messages: at most once, in order per sender, and dead letters for the rest.
- [The death watch ordering guarantee](https://tellus.rs/docs/explanation/death-watch-ordering/): Why receiving Terminated proves that you have seen every message from that actor you will ever see.
- [Membership and downing](https://tellus.rs/docs/explanation/membership-and-downing/): How tellus nodes agree on who belongs to the cluster, decide that a node is gone, and where that agreement ends.
- [Supervision and lifecycle](https://tellus.rs/docs/explanation/supervision-and-lifecycle/): How actors start, fail, restart and terminate, and in which order their resources are released.
- [Event sourcing](https://tellus.rs/docs/explanation/event-sourcing/): How event-sourced actors persist, recover and evolve, and what tellus guarantees about it.

## API reference

- [tellus on docs.rs](https://docs.rs/tellus/latest/tellus/): The complete API documentation, with all features enabled.
- [tellus-persistence-postgres on docs.rs](https://docs.rs/tellus-persistence-postgres/latest/tellus_persistence_postgres/): `PostgresStore`, the PostgreSQL event and snapshot store.
- [tellus-bootstrap-dns on docs.rs](https://docs.rs/tellus-bootstrap-dns/latest/tellus_bootstrap_dns/): `DnsSeeds`, seed discovery from DNS SRV or A/AAAA records.
- [tellus-bootstrap-k8s on docs.rs](https://docs.rs/tellus-bootstrap-k8s/latest/tellus_bootstrap_k8s/): `K8sSeeds`, seed discovery from Kubernetes pods by label selector.
- [tellus-cluster-inspect on docs.rs](https://docs.rs/tellus-cluster-inspect/latest/tellus_cluster_inspect/): An axum router serving a node's cluster state as JSON and server-sent events.
- [Examples](https://github.com/tellus-rs/tellus/tree/main/tellus/examples): The compiled examples behind the tutorials and how-to guides.

## Optional

- [Internals](https://github.com/tellus-rs/tellus/tree/main/docs): Design documentation of the actor runtime, persistence and the cluster, for contributors.
- [Benchmarks](https://tellus.rs/tellus/comparison/): Comparison benchmarks against kameo and ractor.
- [Articles](https://heikoseeberger.de/tags/tellus/): Blog posts about the design of tellus.
